question: In a circuit with a NTC type thermistor and a fixed resistor connected in series connected to a DC power supply, what will happen to the output voltage if there is a rise in temperature?

options.text: The output voltage will fluctuate depending on the resistor value.
The output voltage will remain constant.

solution:
The correct answer is __The output voltage will increase.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• NTC Thermistor__ stands for Negative Temperature Coefficient thermistor.
 
• In an NTC thermistor, the resistance decreases as the temperature increases.
 
• When the thermistor's resistance decreases, the voltage drop across it reduces, causing the output voltage to increase.
 
• The circuit's output voltage depends on the voltage divider principle, where the voltage is distributed based on the resistance values.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Fixed Resistor:**
 
 
• A fixed resistor maintains a constant resistance regardless of temperature or voltage changes.
 
• It helps in setting the output voltage in combination with the thermistor.
 
 
 
• **Voltage Divider Circuit: **
 
 
• The combination of an NTC thermistor and a fixed resistor forms a voltage divider circuit.
 
• The output voltage is split between the thermistor and the fixed resistor based on their resistance values.
 
 
 
• **NTC Thermistor Applications:**
 
 
• Used in temperature sensing circuits.
 
• Commonly found in electronic devices for overheating protection.
